pillars.note: No direct fire-safety pillar. The five stated objectives are about cool-flame behavior, helium dilution, extinction and soot; the PSI SubResearch Area is 'Droplets'. The Research Impacts text mentions only a general support for 'the design of safer spacecraft systems', and its main applications are engines and fuels. Helium dilution and flame extinction are context for suppression research, but no cited line studies a suppressant. The folder name 'suppression' in knowledgeBase/ is the project's own grouping, not a source statement. Pillar list left empty on purpose; the reviewer should decide.

evidence.quote: 1) Examine the combustion behavior of n-dodecane and mixtures of n-dodecane/iso-dodecane at pressures ranging from 0.25 atm to 5 atm.
2) Analyze the effects of helium dilution on cool flame behavior.
Comment[SubResearch Area] Droplets
support the design of safer spacecraft systems by refining knowledge of combustion in microgravity environments.
3) Examine the behavior of combustion characteristics.
4) Investigate the relationship between droplet size, pressure, and flame extinction, and (5) understand the consequence of soot formation during cool flame combustion.
A basic understanding of cool flames is important for understanding ignition phenomena of practical fuels and fuel additives.
Microgravity Investigation

nominal_atmosphere.note: Pressure only, converted at 14.6959 psi/atm. The Science Final Report lists the experiments performed at 0.5 to 5 atm (p. 6). The PSI record is inconsistent: its Objective says 0.25 to 5 atm and its Approach says the gas system delivers mixtures 'ranging from 0.25 to 0.5 atm'; the 0.25 atm bound is an objective that the flown list does not include, so it is not used. The experimental table carries per-test pressure and the O2/N2/He fractions.
